# Rank-four dimension-uniform boundary exclusion

24 October 2026. This is a new theorem extending the previous rank-three tightness result. It depends on the Kraus-span trichotomy proved in wh3_rank_four_kernel_obstruction.md and independently confirmed by the challenge worker. The historical rank-three proofs are unchanged.

## Theorem

Let R_n be arbitrary finite reference spaces, with no common dimension bound. Let X_n be faithful normalized states on C3 tensor R_n and let ξ_n be normalized states on the same spaces with rank ξ_n<=4. If ||X_n-ξ_n||_1 tends to zero, then

limsup_n Tr exp[2(W3 tensor id)(log X_n)-I tensor log (X_n)_R]<=1/3.

Equivalently, for every ε>0 there exists δ(ε)>0, independent of reference dimension, such that every faithful X within trace norm δ(ε) of the rank-at-most-four states has Φ(X)<=1/3+ε. This gives existence, not an explicit or effective numerical modulus.

If Φ(X_n) tends to 1/3, the approximants ξ_n must approach the union of the two previously identified saturation families: I3/3 tensor a pure reference state, and local-unitary images of the normalized antisymmetric rank-three projection. Thus no genuinely rank-four limit state saturates.

## 1. The exact dependency: rank-four Kraus-span geometry

For an output support P of dimension at most four, put

K=ker[2(W3 tensor id)(I-P)].

Its WH Kraus span S(K) lies in P. The referenced algebraic trichotomy states that dim S(K)<=4 implies at least one of:

(a) dim K<=1;
(b) K has a common physical support of dimension at most two;
(c) K is contained in C3 tensor a fixed reference line.

The coordinate transformations in that proof classify vector spaces only. No nonunitary reference filtering is used as an entropy invariance in the present argument.

For every normalized Y supported in K, define F(Y)=S(Y)+S(Y_R)-2S((W3 tensor id)Y). Each branch yields F(Y)<=-log 3:

- In (a), Y is pure. Its Schmidt weights λ give
  -F(Y)=2 log 2+sum_i[λ_i log λ_i-(1-λ_i)log(1-λ_i)]>=log 3.
  Equality requires uniform Schmidt rank three.
- In (b), the exact support-two channel decomposition is, up to local unitaries,
  (W3 tensor id)(Y)=(1/2)UYU-adjoint direct-sum (1/2)Y_R.
  Therefore S(output)=log 2+[S(Y)+S(Y_R)]/2 and F(Y)=-log 4 exactly.
- In (c), Y=A tensor |v><v|. The same scalar eigenvalue inequality gives 2S(W3(A))-S(A)>=log 3, with equality only at A=I3/3.

# A general rank-four boundary obstruction from skew-matrix geometry

24 October 2026, root derivation; independent challenge requested. This is not the previously closed SU(2)-invariant example. Its proposed scope is every output support of dimension at most four.

For a subspace K of C3 tensor R define its WH Kraus span
 S(K)=span{(L_i tensor I)psi:psi in K,i=1,2,3},
where L_i span all complex antisymmetric3×3 matrices. Suppose dim S(K)<=4.
Then at least one of the following holds:
1. dim K<=1;
2. K has a common physical support of dimension at most two;
3. K is contained in C3 tensor a fixed reference line.

## Algebraic proof

Represent vectors by3×r matrices M. If M has rank at least two, the map A→AM from the3D space of skew matrices is injective. For two independent such vectors M,N, each Kraus span has dimension three, so the intersection has dimension at least two.

First suppose M has rank three. Replace an independent N by M+epsilon N if necessary so it too has rank three. Two independent skew matrices A1,A2 satisfy Ai N in S(M). In reference coordinates outside M's support, both Ai annihilate every column of N. Distinct nonzero skew3×3 matrices have distinct one-dimensional kernels, so those columns vanish. Restrict to the common3D reference support and multiply on the right by M inverse. This is a dimension-preserving algebraic change of coordinates, NOT an entropy-preserving physical filter. Now M=I and the two skew matrices satisfy
 A_i T=T^T A_i,  T=N M inverse.
Each A_i gives an invariant kernel line for T; on its two-dimensional quotient, the induced T is self-adjoint for a nondegenerate skew form and therefore scalar. Two distinct kernel lines force these scalars to agree and force T to be scalar on the whole3D space. This contradicts independence. Thus a K of dimension at least two cannot contain a Schmidt-rank-three vector.

If K contains a rank-two M, choose physical Schmidt coordinates and a right-invertible reference change so

For any independent N, replace it by M+epsilon N so its rank is two. As above, two skew intersection matrices force N to have no reference columns outside this two-dimensional support. Write

# Independent audit of the rank-four kernel geometry

Let K be a complex linear subspace of C³⊗C^r and identify its vectors
with3×r coefficient matrices. Define S(K)=span{AM: A^T=−A, M in K}.
Assume dim S(K)<=4. Then at least one holds:
(i) dimK<=1;
(ii) every vector of K has a common physical support of dimension<=2;
(iii) K is contained in C³⊗v for one reference vector v.
The proof is algebraic over C; transpose is bilinear, not adjoint.

## Rank-three member
For rank>=2 matrix M, A↦AM is injective on3×3 skew matrices, so
S(M) has dimension3. If independent M,N inK both have rank3, then
S(M)∩S(N) has dimension>=2. Given a rank3 M and any independent N,
replace N by M+epsilon N at a generic nonzero epsilon to ensure rank3.
Use an invertible reference coordinate change to make M=[I3,0].
Two independent skew matrices B satisfy BN inS(M). Their kernels are
distinct lines, hence the columns of N outside M's reference support
vanish. Thus N=[T,0]. The intersection condition says BT=T^TB for
two independent skew B.

For one such B with kernel line span(u), T preserves that line and
induces a self-adjoint map for the nondegenerate alternating form on
C³/span(u). In dimension2 such a map is scalar, so T=λI+u v^T.
For the second B, T=μI+w z^T with independent u,w. If λ≠μ then the
rank3 matrix (λ−μ)I would equal a matrix of rank<=2, impossible.
Thus λ=μ and u v^T=w z^T. Distinct image lines imply both sides zero.
T is scalar, contradicting independence. Hence dimK>=2 excludes rank3.
No orthogonal normal form for complex isotropic kernel lines is used.

## Rank-two member
Normalize M to [[1,0],[0,1],[0,0]], with remaining reference columns zero.
Every independent N can again be replaced by M+epsilon N to have rank2.
The same two-kernel intersection argument removes its outside reference
columns. Write N=[[p,q],[r,s],[t,u]]. The condition AN inS(M) imposes
on the three skew coefficients the matrix
[[0,t,−r], [−u,0,q], [−t,u,p−s]].
Its kernel has dimension>=2, so its rank is<=1. If t≠0, rows1 and3
are independent. If u≠0, rows2 and3 are independent. Consequently
t=u=0. Undoing N↦M+epsilon N proves that every member of K shares
M's physical plane.

statement: For arbitrary finite reference spaces R_n, faithful normalized X_n on C^3 tensor R_n, and states xi_n with rank xi_n <= 4, if ||X_n - xi_n||_1 tends to zero then limsup Tr exp[2(W3 tensor id)(log X_n) - I tensor log (X_n)_R] <= 1/3. Equivalently, each fixed positive gap above 1/3 has a dimension-uniform positive trace-distance from all rank-at-most-four states. The source gives existence, not an explicit or effective modulus.
